seo.h1: Test yourself on frontend interview questions

faq.a: A free site to test yourself on developer interview questions in Frontend, Backend and Full-stack. Each test picks random questions based on your choices, and at the end you see your score with an explanation for every question.

faq.q: What kinds of tests are there?
faq.a: Three tracks: Frontend, Backend and Full-stack. Each has three levels (Junior, Mid, Senior) and an open test, and you can pick topics or your language and framework, 5 to 20 questions, and a time limit if you like.

faq.q: Is it free? Do I need an account?
faq.a: It is completely free, with no sign-up and no email. Pick a track and a level and start.

A 15-question test from the general topics of the track you choose. It starts at Mid, gets harder when you answer right and easier when you answer wrong, and at the end estimates your level: Junior, Mid or Senior.

faq.q: Which topics do the questions cover?
faq.a: Frontend: JavaScript, CSS, HTML, React, Vue, Angular, TypeScript, browser performance and security. Backend: databases and SQL, APIs, architecture and server security, plus Node.js, Python, PHP/Laravel and C#/.NET. Full-stack combines both.

faq.q: How do I compare my score with others?
faq.a: When you finish, your score is ranked against everyone who took the same track and level (or the same track’s open test), and you see what percentage of them you did better than. It shows once there are enough results.

faq.q: Can I share or print my result?
faq.a: Yes. The result page has a ready-made image for LinkedIn, WhatsApp and more, and a button to print your result with the full review. You can type your name before the test to show on it; that is optional.

faq.q: I found a mistake in a question. What should I do?
faq.a: Press "Report a mistake" under the question, during the test or in the result review, pick the type of problem and add a note. We review every report and fix the question.

faq.q: Will new questions and topics be added?
faq.a: Yes. We keep adding new sections and growing the question bank, and we review existing questions based on your reports.

faq.q: Which languages is the site in?
faq.a: Arabic, English and Turkish. Code stays in English, the way you see it at work.
